# Source mismatches reported by the funding renderer (agent a42998df730df58cd), render round 1 — copied verbatim by the coordinator

Rendered source: funding.extended.yaml f4e6e842dfeb55fe2f85ec91f8a07112cc1ead94c006620a9577dc5dc046a907, task_tools.py c50df2791e04c8b4eb8652ff17714472f2882f05c5034c63e8da95307b429ac9. docs/funding/ published (58 docs, DOCS OK).

**One placement call you may want to look at:** a few combination sentences are placed in the computation documents because that is where those parts of the calculation are covered. They are the late-funding "a day taken out on more than one ground is taken out only once", the shortfall "any record-error allowance… any credit cover", and the returned-wire re-send standard sum. They name those quantities without defining them, so the computation documents are not completely silent about the factors.

**Source mismatches (rendered as they stand):**
1. **Per diem clause retired with nothing replacing it for the closing charge.** `funding_ext_per_diem_shortfall.overwrite[0]` and `funding_ext_funding_month_interest.overwrite[0]` both retire the base clause "daily_interest_amount is loan_amount times note_rate percent divided by per_diem_day_count_basis, rounded to per_diem_daily_rounding_decimals" (`funding_per_diem_interest`). The two replacements cover only the shortfall ("prices a per diem shortfall only and never funding-month interest") and the funding-month interest ("For funding-month interest, and never for a per diem shortfall"). That leaves the pricing of the prepaid interest charge collected at closing with no rule in force, even though it is still in use.
2. **Redraw replacements drop parts of the retired clauses.**
   - `funding_ext_redraw_fee_balance.overwrite[0]` retires "the redraw is charged doc_redraw_fee when the reason is the borrower's (a borrower-requested change or a missed signing)". Its replacement carries only the base-price ladder and drops the borrower-reason condition.
   - `overwrite[1]` retires "doc_redraw_fee once per borrower-caused redraw" and drops "once per borrower-caused redraw".
   - Neither replacement says it is limited to the balance, which Larkspur only recovers by setoff after closing.
3. **Redraw records: rule and compute disagree.** `funding_ext_redraw_fee_balance`: the rule says "The redraws a redraw fee balance looks at are the doc redraw fee charges on the closing that no reversal names… the latest of them is the redraw being priced". The compute instead takes the latest doc_redraw_fee charge whether or not a reversal names it (`rd_charged`/`rd_booked`), and counts redraws as charges minus reversals (`rd_count`).
4. **Shortfall payment amount: rule and compute disagree.** `funding_ext_per_diem_shortfall` rule: "The payment is recorded as a prepaid interest charge … with the per diem shortfall as its amount". But the per diem shortfall is defined before the allowances and credit cover, while `result` (and the tool's `interest_amount`) is "what is left is what the borrower pays".
5. **Credit cover reads too broadly.** `funding_ext_per_diem_shortfall` `sf_cutback`/`sf_cover`: the rule says "a credit whose program may pay prepaid items was cut back at closing … by at least the remainder". The compute sums every credit_reduced/exceeds_eligible_costs entry with no link to that credit or to "at closing", and checks prepaid_items against the file's credit program.
6. **Which filing is decided is not pinned down.** `funding_ext_interest_dispute_decision` `dd_filed`/`dd_type`/`dd_named` read the latest filing still marked pending, of any dispute type. Filing records keep "pending" after a decision record exists, so "a borrower's pending per diem overcharge dispute" does not settle which filing is used when there are several.
7. **Fee setoff claims an effect the tool lacks.** `funding_ext_interest_dispute_decision` rule: "the refund is the excess with interest less those fees, which the setoff settles". `decide_prepaid_interest_dispute_44bdf39e` books no fee entry and does not change the closing fee balance. The rule also doesn't say which outcome applies when the setoff takes the whole refund to zero.
8. **Funding-month days compute only matches in one case.** `funding_ext_funding_month_interest` `fm_days`: for a March first payment date it uses `32 - DAYS(fm_chg_through, disbursement_date)`. That matches the rule ("through the last day of the disbursement month") only when the closing charge ends on the last day of the month right before a 31-day disbursement month.
9. **Funds-out check is looser than the rule.** `funding_ext_late_funding_refund` `lf_est_wires`/`lf_out_days`: the rule says "returned through its own error the wire that went out on the estimated funding date". The compute only checks that some wire of the funding amount went out on that date and that some own-error return exists; it doesn't check that the return names that wire.
